summary: Today's decisions hold up after the close. I approved MSM at half size ($8 of the $15 proposed) and rejected VXUS, with the account at 14.7% cash and a neutral stance ahead of the 10-28 Fed decision. MSM filled at $118.72, the menu close, so the roughly 9% stop near $108 is anchored correctly (L1), and the 10-22 8-K 2.02 and 10-K put the next earnings at about 2027-01-06 (L2). MSM closed at about $118.4 (-0.3%), so no thesis damage. It is a small peer of FAST (which closed -1.8%), and the Skeptic and Implicator were right that it adds a second MRO distributor rather than a new sector; the half size reflects that. The VXUS rejection rested on the 200-day break, beta 1.11 and fresh EM stress (Brazil, China AI rout). The market analyst and Skeptic both pointed the same way, and the Fed is a clean reason to wait a day. Equity closed at $600.52 (-$2.65, -0.4%), with the larger drags in tech-adjacent and growth names (MSCI -2.6%, FAST -1.8%, VRSN -1.7%, IDXX -1.6%). The defensives (WMT, KR, DPZ) slipped less and the ETF sleeve was flat to slightly up. The agent is up 0.09% since inception against SPY +0.42% and the shadow portfolio +4.9%. The gap to the shadow comes mostly from names we rejected or did not hold (RRC after the EQT deal, CART, CALX, WDFC), so it is not a verdict on the process after one week. Two process points to own: (1) I am still holding about 13% cash against the owner's wish to be mostly invested within a week, and I have now declined or halved the only two diversifiers offered; the reasons were sound but idle cash is a real cost if the Fed passes quietly. (2) DPZ's invalidation of $274.88 is still anchored to the pre-fill reference close and sits about 13% under the $316.58 fill, which L1 says to re-anchor. I did not fix it today.
lessons: L1 applied correctly again: MSM's stop was set against the actual fill (filled exactly at the $118.72 menu close, so the ~9% distance held). Still open from L1: re-anchor DPZ's invalidation to the $316.58 fill (about $285 for a true 10%) the next time DPZ is reviewed; the current $274.88 is ~13% below entry.

When a proposal's sector claim ('a sector we do not hold') is contradicted by a held peer (MSM vs FAST), judge diversification on economic exposure, not the data label, and size down rather than reject if quality is good. This was the right call for MSM, but the proposer should check held peers before claiming a new sector.

Deferring a non-conviction diversifier (VXUS) one day for a binary event (Fed) is cheap only if the follow-up actually happens; revisit VXUS or another non-US/gold sleeve on 10-28 or 10-29 if it closes back above its 200-day, rather than letting cash sit by default (cash ~13% vs the owner's 'mostly invested within about a week').

Do not read the shadow-portfolio gap (+4.9% vs +0.09%) as evidence against the rejections: it is driven by event-driven moves (RRC +15% on the EQT deal, CART takeover talk) that were unverifiable or merger-arb at decision time. Keep grading decisions on reasoning and information available, and keep the 'idle cash' concern separate from the 'rejected winners' concern.
